question_text: Find the derivative of cos²x from the first principle with respect to x.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the identity that turns a difference of two squared cosines into a product.

steps.label: State the first principle
steps.margin_note: First mark. cos²(x + h) means (cos(x + h))² — the cosine of x + h, then squared.

recall.must_convey: That the first principle is written with f(x) = cos²x and f(x + h) = cos²(x + h).
accept: write the first principle with f of x equal to cos squared x
f of x plus h is cos of x plus h whole squared
take the limit of cos squared x plus h minus cos squared x over h
first principle rasta, cos square of x plus h ani rasta
start from the definition of the derivative

steps.why: The definition is the marked move, and writing f(x + h) correctly as (cos(x + h))² is what keeps the next step available.
common_mistakes: Writing cos²(x + h) as cos²x + cos²h.
steps.memory_tip: cos²x is the cosine first, the square second. Substitute x + h into the angle, then square.

steps.label: Use cos²A − cos²B
steps.margin_note: Second mark. This identity comes from sin(A + B) sin(A − B) = sin²A − sin²B together with sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ. Learn it as it stands: it saves three lines here.
lines: Here A = x + h and B = x, so
A + B = 2x + h  and  A − B = h
cos²(x + h) − cos²x = −sin(2x + h) sin h

recall.must_convey: That cos²A − cos²B = −sin(A + B) sin(A − B) is applied with A = x + h and B = x, giving −sin(2x + h) sin h.
accept: use cos squared a minus cos squared b equals minus sin a plus b sin a minus b
the difference of the two squared cosines becomes a product of two sines
a plus b is two x plus h and a minus b is h
cos square minus cos square formula apply cheyyali
the numerator becomes minus sin of two x plus h into sin h
heard_as: cos squared a minus cos squared b

steps.why: The identity turns a difference of squares into one product in a single line. Factorising as (cos A − cos B)(cos A + cos B) and then using sum-to-product reaches the same place but costs three more lines.
common_mistakes: Using +sin(A + B) sin(A − B), which equals sin²A − sin²B, not cos²A − cos²B.
Squaring the sum-to-product form of cos A − cos B instead of using this identity.
steps.memory_tip: cos²A − cos²B = −sin(A+B) sin(A−B): sines on the right, one minus in front.

steps.label: Arrange sin h over h
steps.margin_note: Third mark. No adjusting factor is needed here — the sine angle is already h. Say so, because the examiner wants the standard limit named.
lines: The angle h matches the denominator, so

recall.must_convey: That the product is separated so (sin h)/h stands alone, and the standard limit is named.
accept: separate sin h over h and use the standard limit
limit of sin h by h is one as h tends to zero
the sine angle is already h so no adjustment is needed
sin h by h standard limit one avuthundi
split the product before taking limits

steps.why: The product splits into a factor that is continuous at h = 0 and a factor that is the standard limit, so each can be evaluated on its own.
common_mistakes: Cancelling sin h against h as though they were equal.
Letting h → 0 inside sin(2x + h) while still keeping h in sin h.
steps.memory_tip: Split the product first, then take limits one factor at a time.

steps.label: Take the limit
steps.margin_note: Last mark. −sin 2x is the compact form. It equals 2 cos x × (−sin x), which is the chain-rule answer — a quick check that the limit work is right.
lines: As h → 0, sin(2x + h) → sin 2x and (sin h)/h → 1

accept: the answer is minus sin two x
sin of two x plus h tends to sin two x so it is minus sin two x
minus sin two x is the same as minus two sin x cos x
answer minus sin two x vasthundi
derivative of cos squared x is minus sin two x

steps.why: The double angle appears because A + B was 2x + h. Checking that −sin 2x equals −2 sin x cos x confirms the identity was used the right way round.
common_mistakes: Giving +sin 2x by dropping the minus from the identity.
Treating −2 sin x cos x as a different answer from −sin 2x.
steps.memory_tip: The answer is −sin 2x. The double angle comes from A + B = 2x + h.
